rules.summary: Analyzer threw an unhandled exception on a single file (escalates to error if failOnAnalyzerError is set).
Over-abstraction and redundant indirection: introducing cross-layer forwardingtrampolines, inverted dependencies, or cycles for trivial commonalities.
File boundary imbalance: multiple high-complexity functions in a single file lacksemantic cohesion, abnormally aggregating responsibilities.
Cross-domain internal penetration: bypassing public export facade contracts to directly access private internal implementations.
Environment configuration leak: pure domain models directly read environment variables or disk configuration files.
Declared configuration property is never referenced in decisions, control flow, orcalculations across the codebase (dead configuration).
Duplicate configuration entries declared across multiple locations, violating single source of truth.
Implicit configuration scatter: business code directly reads environment variables or tuning constants.
Unstructured configuration access: accessing configuration in an unstructured,arbitrary manner across layers without a centralized registry.
Configuration tightly coupled with domain logic: domain models directly bind tospecific config file formats or disk parsers.
Configuration over-abstraction: simple static configuration introduces excessiveunnecessary indirection and forwarding layers.
Flat configuration sprawl antipattern: large volume of configuration files sprawledacross root directory without domain isomorphic hierarchy.
Configuration sub-table routing contract breach: unregistered sub-table detached fromcore routing contract, lacking dot-notation routing.
Polyglot AST parsing and adapter logic must be decoupled into independent adaptermodules; analyzer core must not mix AST construction details.
Core reverse flow: domain layer inversely depends on outer application, infrastructure, or interface layers.
Layer bypass: interface layer controllers bypass application services to directly couple with infrastructure implementations.
Formal layering illusion: directory structure appears separated, but call graphs and data flows violate layer boundaries.
Monolithic dispatchers with excessive branches (> 8) tightly couple domain logic, violating the Open-Closed Principle.
Dispatcher closure fragmentation: Object literal defines excessive inline function closures (>= 15), causing closure explosion and function inflation.
Hollow facade payload and insufficient density: facade module lacks substantive domainorchestration, schema validation, or immutability contracts.
Implicit global mutable state: modules are tightly coupled via top-level global variables or static singletons.
Headless architecture breach: core business logic or calculation modules directly bind to UI/IDE view frameworks.
Responsibility leak: pure domain models directly reference or leak external frameworks (Express, Vue, Godot, ORM).
Layer boundary breach: outer implementations are directly referenced by inner layers (Clean/DDD inverted hierarchy).
Plumbing overhead ratio (POR) exceeds threshold; wiring code dominates logic payload.
File entity role imbalance and pseudo-shared library: file carries excessive mutablestate or coupled logic but is heavily imported as a shared library.
Business module harboring unbounded common capabilities: domain module internally hostsand exports general infrastructure or utilities.
Strategy skeleton candidate: detected complex workflows sharing isomorphicpre-validation and post-execution teardown steps.
Monolithic template renderer coupling: oversized function concatenates deep HTML/SVG/DSL templates without subcomponent decomposition.
Kitchen-sink utility antipattern: detected utils/common dumping ground file accumulatingheterogeneous unstructured logic.
Layering boundary breach in incremental pipeline (clean-layer semantics).
Deeply nested inline callback chains create callback hell, complicate exceptionpropagation, and mask race conditions.
Dense syntactic packing of bitwise, arithmetic and conditional operators without namingor spacing exceeds human cognitive chunking capacity.
Giant expressions with deeply nested ternaries or unbounded logical chains createcognitive overload and obscure branching logic.
Cramming multiple distinct statements or side-effects onto a single line impairs stacktraces, debug stepping, and code readability.
Banner divider (═) used in small file (< 150 lines).
Async exported function lacks concurrency scheduling assumptions, reentrancy, or idempotence contract.
Public exported symbol lacks Docstring/JSDoc description, parameters, or return type documentation.
Tautological redundant comment merely repeating symbol or function name.
Source file missing top-level file header comment explaining responsibility and design intent.
Standard strict six-field file header missing one of six mandatory fields (Module, File Path, Architecture Role, Dependencies & Triggers, Responsibilities, Exit Semantics & Design Rationale).
File header declared path does not match actual physical file path.
File layout order violation: top-level six-field module header comment must precede all non-directive code statements.
Documented contract (pure, side-effect free, thread-safe) contradicts actual AST data flow or side effects.
Comment language deviates from dominant project or domain standard.
Unordered interleaving of languages in comments within a single file.
Encoding corruption detected (U+FFFD replacement characters, UTF-8 decoded as Latin-1, or Windows-1252 mojibake).
Inconsistent section separator styles mixed in same file (short ── title ── vs long ──── title).
Comment or docstring contains non-factual terminology, casual phrasing, hyperbolic assertions, or emotional slurs.
Low semantic comment density or verbatim line-by-line translation without explaining intent.
Comment or docstring physical line length exceeds 100 columns.
Multiple homogeneous unextracted literals (status codes, protocols, paths, events) in the same call scope should be clustered and extracted together.
Homogeneous semantic constants across files have naming splits or minor value drifts, violating single source of truth (SSOT).
Module-level constants must be placed in the primary declaration section immediately following imports, not scattered within functions or business logic.
Type definitions, interfaces, and contract shapes must be declared before core functions and business logic classes.
Large volumes of constants are scattered across business files without a structured, tiered constant library.
Shared constant ownership is misclassified; avoid dumping constants into kitchen-sink files or hiding them in private modules.
Local invariants, lazily initialized values, or short-lived resources must not be needlessly hoisted to module scope.
Multiple identical local literals in a function should be consolidated as local constants at the function header.
Complexity amplification trap: blocking I/O or serialization implicitly nested initeration or hot call chains.
Elastic complexity budget exceeded based on comprehensive language, role, scope, and clarity metrics.
Artificial splitting gaming: artificially deflating complexity by generatingexcessive single-line pass-through forwarding functions.
Uncontrolled complexity without architectural justification: high complexityoriginates from chaotic nesting and responsibility piling.
Uncontrolled deep control flow nesting: control flow nesting level exceeds elasticbudget for context type (business > 3, state machine > 5).
Deep long-span control flow escape: unstructured control flow escape(return/break/throw) executed in deep nesting (>= 4) far from function header.
Recursive or mutually recursive call chain without guaranteed termination guards across functions/files.
Distributed redundant complexity: highly similar algorithms, calculations, orvalidations scattered across multiple files creating latent complexity.
Unbounded transient memory allocation and repeated full materialization inside hot loops.
State machine dispatch structure standard: single branch within state machinebranches exceeds 30 LOC, degrading dispatch skeleton clarity.
Unbounded polynomial time complexity across function/file boundaries: nestediteration call chains incur prohibitive overhead.
Tautological loop traversal detected with zero or negligible state mutation entropy delta.
Redundant defensive validations within trusted internal domain boundaries.
Data access abstraction leak: business core directly manipulates persistence drivers or storage details.
N+1 query pattern and repeated storage calls within iteration or mapping contexts.
Unbounded data retrieval or full-table in-memory filtering in online request paths.
Resource registry bidirectional mapping inconsistency or dangling asset: resourcecenter contains empty paths or dangling references.
Repeated serialization and deserialization cycles across internal call chains.
Development-only dependency imported in production code: devDependencies package imported without type-only qualifier.
Dependency inversion violation: lower-level infrastructure or common modulesinversely depend on high-level business modules.
Function-scoped lazy import without audit declaration or documented rationale.
High-risk restrictive or viral copyleft license (AGPL/GPL) dependency introduced in proprietary/commercial domain.
Deprecated or unmaintained package imported: third-party library is officially unmaintained or superseded by standard capabilities.
File layout and import grouping do not conform to modern polyglot engineering standards.
File layout order violation: top-level import statement declared after contract types, constants, or business logic statements.
Import of undeclared external package (phantom dependency) not listed in project manifests (package.json, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml).
Unpinned or wildcard dependency version: external package declared with floating wildcard (*, latest, open range) in project manifest.
Scattered hardcoded unmanaged external URLs, file paths, or connection strings in business logic.
Import of known-malicious, compromised, or severely vulnerable third-party package identified in supply chain integrity registry.
Wildcard import impairs explicit dependency tracking and tree-shaking optimization.
Declarative import boundary violation: cross-group dependency or unauthorized external package import.
Duplicate content lines (>= 24 chars) detected in documentation.
Unclosed Markdown code fence detected.
Backtick path or relative link points to non-existent file.
Documentation prose contains promotional slogans, hyperbolic claims, or unstandardized milestone jargon.
Identical literal frequency exceeds threshold in the same file (default >= 3 occurrences).
Unhandled floating promise: asynchronous operation executed without await, return, void, or .catch() error handler.
Vague or empty error diagnostic message: thrown error lacks actionable diagnostic context, root cause details, or troubleshooting hints.
Error code re-thrown across declarations or propagating through excessive call stack hops.
Expensive deep copy (.duplicate(true)) or blocking serialization/IO executed inside a loop.
Pre-commit gate lacks AST staged slice complexity and nesting budget check (CC <= 15, Depth <= 4).
Pre-commit gate runs unconstrained whole-repo test suites without staged-file filtering, risking budget overrun.
Gate script lacks strict error termination flags, risking silent failures and false-positive gate passes.
Gate pipeline lacks static validation for facade substantive bearing (ELOC >= 15) and vacuous forwarding elimination.
Repository lacks local left-shift Git hooks; all defect feedback relies solely on remote CI.
Pre-commit gate does not enforce physical hygiene: lacks zero-byte empty file detection.
Dual-tier gate boundary is not isomorphic; remote CI checks are not mirrored in local hooks.
Gate system lacks structured commit-msg validation for Conventional Commits and anti-jargon hygiene.
Commit-msg gate does not enforce bidirectional bilingual style terms constraints (commit-msg-forbidden-terms.json unwired).
Monorepo commit message gate lacks [Project] section or whitelist verification.
Dual-platform gate scripts are not paired; missing corresponding .sh or .ps1 gate implementation.
PowerShell gate script uses interactive prompts without output redirection guard.
Git hook router invokes fragile shell or Windows PS 5.1 directly without cross-platform safety fallback.
Gate system lacks single-source-of-truth rule catalog verification, risking rule drift.
Repository completely lacks a gate defense system (no Git hooks and no CI pipeline detected).
Presentation layer directly manipulates bare ProgressBar instance, bypassing KStatusBar standard animations.
Presentation view directly couples with backend domain singletons or cross-layer global EventBus subscriptions.
Legacy Godot 3 signal connect signature passing method name as a string.

Legacy Godot 3 export statement detected.
Presentation main view controller does not inherit from BaseScreen or BaseModal base class.

Presentation UI text hardcodes raw strings without UIIntermediary or i18n translation key binding.

Presentation view script line count exceeds physical budget limit (LOC <= 450 lines).

Legacy onready keyword detected.
Pooled object does not implement or invoke reset_state contract upon acquisition or release.
Deprecated Pool*Array type detected.

Legacy remote/master/puppet/slave function modifiers detected.

context.Context is not the first parameter of the function.
Error return value silently discarded with blank identifier (_).
Method receiver naming does not adhere to Go conventions.
Error variable is not prefixed with err.

Concurrent modifications by multiple agents produce architectural boundary breaches,cross-module dependency cycles, or contract incompatibilities.

Empty catch blocks silently swallow exceptions, causing silent data corruption ormasking critical failures. A catch whose body carries an explicit rationale marker(best-effort / ignore / intentional / expected) is treated as a documented decisioninstead of a silent swallow.
Naked `.unwrap()` causes unrecoverable process panics in production upon Err or None.
Pseudo-catch blocks containing only dummy non-handling statements (void 0, deadassignment) silently swallow exceptions without logging or documented rationale.
Inconsistent file naming causes cross-platform casing issues and impairs modular discovery.
Substantial production modules must declare their architectural role and responsibility boundary.
Anti-gaming violation: artificial function splitting, tautological test padding, orempty boilerplate gaming quality metrics.
Deeply nested control flows (> 5 levels) create high cognitive load and increase defect risk.
Vacuous wrapper methods that purely forward calls without validation or translation addunnecessary indirection.
Deep class inheritance hierarchies (> 2 levels) introduce fragile base class problems;composition is preferred.
Domain layer must remain clean and portable; importing UI or CLI presentation frameworksintroduces severe coupling.
Underlying diagnostic messages and remediations must use standard English centrallymanaged by constant dictionaries, prohibiting hardcoded non-ASCII or inline stringsat emitter sites.
Performing invariant I/O, regex construction, or repetitive configuration lookups inloops incurs severe CPU/throughput penalties.
Calling linear search (.find / .indexOf / .includes) inside a loop scales at O(N*M);pre-indexing in Map/Set optimizes to O(N).
Numeric timer delays bypass centralized clamping; a literal of <=0 triggers a ~1ms busyloop (CPU/IO hotspot).
Sync fs calls block the host event loop (UI jank in IDE extensions, request stalls on servers).
Calling array linear lookups (.includes / .indexOf) inside loops creates quadraticO(N*M) overhead; pre-indexing into a Set hoisted outside the loop optimizesmembership tests to O(1).

Static review rule identifier drift or hallucination: mentioned rule ID is notregistered in the single-source rule catalog.
Transient task tags and batch jargon (pXX/phaseXX/stXX/wip) compromise architecturallongevity and create documentation drift.
Objective technical language guard: text contains promotional rhetoric, absolute claims,emotional disparagement, or process buzzwords.
AST slice mutation introduces breaking signature drift or uncontained side-effectspropagating across external call chains.
Redundant if-then-else returning boolean literals increases cyclomatic complexity and mental overhead.
Legacy constructs (e.g. `var` in modern TS/JS, dead `pass` in GDScript) violate language idiomatic standards.
Historical trajectory exhibits cyclic regressions, flip-flop oscillations, orre-introduces previously eliminated architectural anti-patterns.
Implicit loose typing hides type errors at runtime and weakens static safety guarantees.
Unannotated function signatures compromise API boundaries and allow unintended type drift.
Naked `any` bypasses the entire compiler type checker, leaking type instability.
Passing or assigning `undefined as any` or `null as any` indicates an InterfaceSegregation Principle (ISP) violation.
Accessing properties via `(expr as any).prop` bypasses compiler type safety andindicates missing type narrowing guards.
Exported functions, classes, and public methods must specify explicit return types toprotect public API contracts.
Multiple nested loops create potential O(N^2)/O(N^3) complexity hotspots or implicit linear searches.
Function cyclomatic complexity exceeds threshold.
High-entropy string detected, suspected of being a secret credential or API token.
Local variable or parameter shadows Python built-in name.
Duplicated code clone detected across multiple lines based on rolling polynomial hash.
Unreachable dead code detected after terminating control flow (return, throw, break, raise).
Zero-byte empty file, blank comment-only file, or hollow shell file lacking AST semantic payload.
Physical line endings contract violation (PowerShell scripts must be CRLF, other source files must be LF).
Exception variable in except clause is not named exc.
File naming convention distortion (kebab-case for TS/JS, snake_case for GDScript/Python/Rust).
Single-letter variable name in business logic (only loop indices i/j/k and discard _ allowed).
Temporary stub markers (`TODO`, `FIXME`, `XXX`, `HACK`) lingering in code or comments.
Temporary construction phase jargon (`pXX`, `phaseXX`, `stXX`, `wip`) leaking into code or comments.
Unannotated compiler or linter suppression directive (@ts-ignore, @ts-nocheck, eslint-disable, # noqa) without approved exemption.
Vacuous passthrough wrapper functions forwarding arguments directly without added value degrade effective code density.
Redundant zero-argument forwarding wrappers trivially delegating to inner targets without validation, transformation, or abstraction.
Module-level cyclic dependency detected (covering Python relative imports and package resolution).
File physical line count or function count exceeds architecture threshold.
Transient heap allocation inside a loop (ADV-PRF-002), violating the zero-transient-allocation contract.
Backward compatibility shim, redundant legacy alias, or outdated parameter forwarding detected.
Invocation or access of deprecated symbol detected in internal production source code.
Cross-generational fallback chain or redundant fallback cascade detected in non-perimeter source code.
Identifier contains cryptic, incomplete, or non-standard abbreviations harming code readability.
Collections (Array/Set) should use plural nouns or List suffixes; mappings (Map/Dict) should express key-to-value relationships.
Identifier length inflation (30-40+ characters) or multiple symbols sharing long prefixes indicates insufficient modular decomposition.
Source directory names must be lowercase kebab-case or single words; CamelCase, spaces, and temporary phase words are prohibited.
File names must follow target language conventions (kebab-case for TS/JS, snake_case for Python/Rust/GDScript) and contain no temporary construction jargon.
Module-level immutable constants must adhere to UPPER_SNAKE_CASE naming conventions.
Mutable let or var declarations at module scope are prohibited (avoid implicit global shared mutable state).
Engineering assets and test suites must not contain construction phase or temporary jargon markers (phase numbers, temporary tokens, `wip` markers).
Variable identifier length is outside acceptable bounds (excessively short or excessively long).
Function or method identifier length is too short to communicate its operational responsibility.
Class properties, object fields, and methods must follow camelCase naming conventions.
Structured resource repositories (constants, strings, rules, configs) are overly broad and bloated, requiring decomposition by domain.
Over-fragmentation in structured resource repositories where tiny files use 3-level deep names; consolidate into parent domain.
Resource repository naming depth exceeds limit (maximum 3 tiers: base type + functional domain + optional subdomain).
Resource repository file name has excessive descriptive word stacking, creating maintenance burden.
Resource repository file responsibility mismatch (declared as pure constant library but contains substantial executable functions/classes).
Single-letter variable names in business logic are prohibited (exemptions: loop counters and discard symbols).
Type definitions, interfaces, and class declarations must follow PascalCase naming conventions.
Vague or meaningless generic variable names (such as bare data, res, ret, tmp, item) are prohibited.
Redundant constant nesting: indirect constant aliases, deep constant objects, or pseudo-constants in nested scopes.
Lossy precision rounding or mismatched scaling detected in mathematical calculationpath, risking IEEE 754 drift.
Deep nested loops (>= 3 levels) detected, creating potential O(N^3) computational hotspots.
Linear collection scan antipattern in loop: performing linear searches(find/includes/has/in list) inside loops degrading complexity to O(N*M).
Synchronous blocking I/O invoked inside async context or high-frequency frame loop.
Unbounded collection growth inside loop or timer, risking O(t) or O(n) memory leaks.
Transient heap allocation inside high-frequency loop (new Array, new Object, .duplicate(true)).
Transient heap allocation in high-load hot paths; object pooling required (ADV-PRF-002).
Hot path expensive resources lack reuse pooling: frequent allocation of heavy objects,buffers, or connections in loops or hot calls.
